transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Anna (BluePeak Head of ML), Jonas (BluePeak SecEng), Priya (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 6-week pilot to validate prompt sanitization and prompt storage retention controls plus end-to-end latency/cost benchmarks. Primary ask: ensure no PII persists past configurable retention, support optional on-prem encryption of prompt blobs, and a benchmark pass at 95th perc latency < 450ms for typical 512-token flows.

Topics:
- Success criteria (PII removal, retention, latency/cost targets)
- Workload sizing (qps, sequence lengths, burst patterns)
- Benchmarks & measurement windows (24-72h)
- Data handling (redaction, prompt storage, KMS/HSM, audit logs)
- Timeline and resources for a POC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Maya, AE for Redwood Inference, and Liam's our solutions engineer. We'll run through what BluePeak wants to validate in the pilot and then sketch a bench plan.
[00:22] Anna (BluePeak): Hi, thanks. Main thing for us is provable PII removal. The models for patient triage take free-text notes, so we need no patient-identifiers stored after processing. also retention windows are legal reqs for some markets.
[00:41] Jonas (BluePeak SecEng): yeah and we need auditability. can you do KMS-wrapped prompt blobs? We have an HSM in our VPC.
[00:58] Liam (Redwood SE): short answer yes. Redwood Private can integrate with customer K M S and HSMs, we support key wrapping on prompt-at-rest. For hosted POC we can demo envelope encryption and show the key lifecycle docs. note: sometimes transcription shows K V cache as K V cash in our logs, but that's a UI label we can fix.
[01:25] Priya (BluePeak PM): on success criteria - we want three things: 1) no PII persisted beyond N hours, 2) latency under threshold for 95th perc, and 3) cost per 1k tokens within our target.
[01:47] Maya: Can you quantify traffic? qps, typical sequence length, bursts?
[01:54] Anna: baseline is 8 qps average, with peak bursts to 120 qps for short periods during morning triage. token length distribution: median 180 tokens, 95th at 520.
[02:14] Liam: ok that's helpful. For the benchmark we'll simulate 24-72 hours with the same burst profile. We'll propose a pilot cluster of 4 A100-style GPUs for the dedicated test run, with autoscale headroom. that should hit your peak and give us margin to measure throughput and SLOs.
[02:45] Jonas: i want to confirm: redaction — is that inline (we strip on ingest) or do you store original and redact later?
[02:55] Liam: both options are supported. recommended flow for this POC: inline sanitization pipeline that strips PII before it's written to any persistent prompt store. We also provide a redaction log for audit that contains only hashes and redaction reasons — no raw PII. note: sometimes our auto-transcript calls it "sanitation" not "sanitization" — minor naming quirk.
[03:20] Maya: for legal and compliance we can share our redaction whitepaper plus a sample retention policy template.
[03:34] Anna: retention settings - we need per-tenant retention override. can you set retention to 0 for certain namespaces?
[03:43] Liam: yes, retention is configurable per namespace/route. For POC we can set BluePeak-prod-1 to immediate purge after processing (0 hours) and keep an audit trail for 30 days with only digests.
[03:58] Priya: how do you prove deletion? do you provide deletion logs or forensic proof?
[04:06] Liam: we emit deletion events with timestamps and KMS key rotations. On Private we can provide the physical scrub scripts; on hosted we'll provide deletion proof and optionally a third-party attestation window.
[04:22] Anna: good. next: prompt storage — we want to avoid storing prompts as-is in S3-like buckets unless encrypted.
[04:32] Liam: by default we encrypt at rest; we can also enable hashed prompt indices so the raw prompt isn't stored, only a one-way hash for de-dupe. if you want zero-storage, we can do ephemeral KV-cache only for the duration of the request and never persist to blobstore. that impacts debugging and evals though.
[04:58] Jonas: debugging is important for the first 2-3 weeks. can we have a debug mode where prompts are stored in an isolated bucket w/ short TTL and strict RBAC?
[05:10] Maya: yes that's common. pilot plan: enable debug storage for 14 days with strict RBAC and KMS control, then switch to ephemeral mode. we'll capture request IDs and redaction diffs for investigations.
[05:27] Anna: benchmarks — how do we measure latency and cost?
[05:33] Liam: we'll run two passes: synthetic load using your prompt sets to emulate qps/bursts and an end-to-end run with real traffic if you can sanction it. measure 95th perc latency, p50, p99, and tokens-per-second per GPU. cost will be modeled from actual GPU hours + token rates for hosted run.
[05:55] Priya: is the 95th perc target of 450ms realistic? our current infra is around 600-700 on a smaller model.
[06:06] Liam: depends on model variant. for a quantized 7B with batching and KV cache optimizations we can likely hit sub-450ms for 512 tokens single-turn on dedicated infra; but for longer contexts or more recent LLMs, you may see higher latencies. we will include a model-variant fallback plan: if latency too high we'll route to a lower-cost variant with shorter context to maintain SLOs.
[06:34] Anna: that fallback sounds ok, but we need to define correctness regressions threshold. if fallback reduces quality we want automatic rollback.
[06:43] Liam: agreed — will add a quality regression check tied to golden prompt tests; rollback/alert if metric drops >2% (configurable).
[06:55] Maya: timeline? you asked for 6 weeks pilot. we propose: week 0 scoping and infra + access, week 1-2 bench prep and dry runs, week 3 24-72h heavy benchmark, week 4-5 iterate on redaction and retention, week 6 wrap + report.
[07:19] Priya: resource ask from us?
[07:22] Liam: a VPC peering or temporary VPN for Private demo (if you choose private), 3 representative prompt sets, and a low-sensitivity slice of traffic for end-to-end run.
[07:34] Jonas: security review — SSO? we use Okta, SAML 2.0.
[07:39] Maya: Redwood supports SAML/Okta and SCIM for provisioning. We'll send SSO setup guide.
[07:45] Anna: audit logs — we need retention for 1 year stored in our region. possible?
[07:51] Liam: yes, logs can be exported to your cloud storage; retention and region are configurable for Private. For hosted we can support export hooks to your bucket.
[08:03] [10:00] CROSSTALK briefly about deck links and a shared benchmark sheet
[10:15] Anna: curious about on-prem option — our compliance team might require on-prem host for production, but pilot can be hosted if we have strong KMS control.
[10:25] Liam: pilot hosted with customer KMS integration is common. On-prem package includes air-gapped installer and audit scripts if you decide to move to that later.
[10:40] Priya: what about token redaction — do you drop PII before model prompt concatenation or after?
[10:48] Liam: before. we run a redaction/sanitization step as the first middleware; if redaction fails we fail the request or route to a manual review queue based on policy.
[11:04] Jonas: can the redaction classifier be tuned with our data?
[11:10] Liam: yes, we can ingest your labeled examples to improve redaction quality for the pilot. that would be part of scope; training is lightweight (few-shot fine-tune or rule updates) and we keep the models for redaction separate from the primary LLM.
[11:28] Anna: success criteria recap — no raw PII in persistent stores, ability to set retention to 0 for namespaces, audit logs with deletion events, 95th perc latency < 450ms for 512 tokens during benchmark, cost estimate within target.
[11:45] Maya: correct. we'll put that in the POC doc and include acceptance test cases.
[12:00] Priya: what about monitoring — can we get per-route cost breakdowns?
[12:07] Liam: yes Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency, and tokens-per-second. we can provide a dashboard link during pilot and give CSV exports.
[12:20] Anna: one more: are you able to anonymize logs to feed into our analytics without leaking PII?
[12:28] Liam: yes, we can provide aggregated metrics and hashed identifiers. raw logs can be redacted before export.
[12:36] Maya: any blockers from your side to start?
[12:40] Anna: we need legal to review an example DPA and redaction clause. rest is internal approvals.
[12:48] Maya: we'll attach a sample DPA and redaction clause with the next email.
[12:55] [20:00] brief pause while Maya and team share doc links in chat
[20:22] Liam: technical note — for the benchmark we'll instrument KV cache hit rates, batching efficiency, and memory pressure per GPU. those three metrics explain most cost/latency behavior.
[20:39] Jonas: do you support quantized model variants? we want lower cost variants we can fallback to.
[20:45] Liam: yes, quantized paths supported; Redwood Optimize will recommend a quantization profile for your workload. note: quantization can change tokenization edge cases so we'll include golden prompts in the regression suite.
[21:03] Anna: ok. how will you demonstrate deletion during pilot to satisfy our audit?
[21:10] Liam: we'll run deletion tests and provide deletion events + cryptographic proof of erasure (hash plus timestamp) and an exported manifest. for Private we can run the actual erase scripts in your environment.
[21:26] Priya: what does success look like for us at the end?
[21:30] Anna: defined acceptance tests pass, bench numbers within target, legal sign off on retention and DPA.
[21:36] Maya: perfect. summary of immediate next steps: Maya sends security + DPA; Liam sends POC infra plan and bench sheet; customer provides prompt sets and short traffic slice. schedule bench window week of 5/25.
[21:56] [52:00] Wrap up and thanks, quick handoffs in chat.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels auto-substituted; a few acronyms transcribed as spaced letters (e.g., S A M L). There are a handful of misheard words (K V cache -> K V cash), but technical intent preserved.
